answer: Accounts whose stake arrived through the same funding wharf, the on-ramp address that first paid them, share one reward cap of 100 POA per epoch. A lone account keeps all 100; 1,000 sybils split it to 0.1 each while each still posts a 5 POA bond, a net loss of about 4,900 POA. Any auditor can trace the dune of shared deposits in the funding graph, and a randomness beacon picks who audits; hidden shared ancestry burns every linked bond. Colluders cannot pool, since each needs its own seasoned wharf. Honest single-wallet users never hit the cap.
